walkthrough:
Set the curve and line equations equal to find intersection points:
$$4x^{1/2} - 2x = 3 - x \implies x - 4x^{1/2} + 3 = 0$$

Treat the equation as a quadratic in terms of $u = x^{1/2}$:
$$u^2 - 4u + 3 = 0 \implies (u - 1)(u - 3) = 0$$
$$u = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad u = 3$$

Square each root to find the $x$-coordinates:
$$x^{1/2} = 1 \implies x = 1$$
$$x^{1/2} = 3 \implies x = 9$$
$$\text{Coordinates: } x = 1, \quad x = 9$$

Evaluate the gradient at the $x$-coordinate of $B$ ($x = 1$):
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=1} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{1}} - 2 = 2 - 2 = 0$$

Conclude that $B$ is a stationary point:
$$\text{Since } \frac{dy}{dx} = 0 \text{ at } x = 1, \, B \text{ is a stationary point on the curve}$$

hints: Line $y = 3-x$ crosses $x$-axis at $x = 3$ and meets curve at $C(9,-6)$.
Calculate triangle area under $x$-axis from line: $\frac{1}{2}(9-3)(6) = 18$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of the triangular region under the $x$-axis formed by the line $y = 3 - x$ from its $x$-intercept $(3,0)$ to intersection $C(9, -6)$:
$$\text{Base} = 9 - 3 = 6, \quad \text{Height} = |-6| = 6$$
$$\text{Area}_{\text{triangle}} = \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 6 = 18$$

Integrate the curve equation $y = 4x^{1/2} - 2x$ between $x = 4$ (point $A$) and $x = 9$ (point $C$):
$$\int_4^9 \left( 4x^{1/2} - 2x \right)\,dx = \left[ \frac{4x^{3/2}}{3/2} - x^2 \right]_4^9 = \left[ \frac{8}{3}x^{3/2} - x^2 \right]_4^9$$

Evaluate the definite integral across the limits:
$$\text{At } x = 9: \quad \frac{8}{3}(27) - 81 = 72 - 81 = -9$$
$$\text{At } x = 4: \quad \frac{8}{3}(8) - 16 = \frac{64}{3} - 16 = \frac{16}{3}$$
$$\int_4^9 (4x^{1/2} - 2x)\,dx = -9 - \frac{16}{3} = -\frac{43}{3} = -14\frac{1}{3}$$

Subtract the magnitude of the curve area from the triangle area to determine the shaded region:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 18 - 14\frac{1}{3} = 3\frac{2}{3} \quad \left(\text{or } \frac{11}{3}\right)$$
